professor.name: Dr. Hughes
professor.text: Many companies now track how productive employees are when they work from home, for example by monitoring computer activity. Is this reasonable, or does it go too far? Explain your view.

students.name: Marcus
students.text: I think some monitoring is reasonable. Companies pay for the work, so they need a way to make sure people are actually working.

students.name: Elena
students.text: It goes too far. Measuring clicks doesn't show real productivity, and it destroys trust between managers and employees.

professor.name: Professor Lindqvist
professor.text: Some educators argue that grades should be replaced with written feedback, because grades make students focus on scores rather than learning. Do you agree? Why or why not?

students.name: Tariq
students.text: I agree. When I get only a number, I don't know what to improve. Detailed feedback would help me much more.

students.name: Sophie
students.text: Grades are still necessary. Universities and employers need a simple way to compare students.

professor.name: Dr. Chen
professor.text: Cities around the world are introducing fees for cars entering the city center. Is this a fair way to reduce traffic and pollution? Explain your opinion.

students.name: Lukas
students.text: Yes. Drivers who cause traffic and pollution should pay for it, and the money can improve public transport.

students.name: Amara
students.text: It isn't fair to people with lower incomes who live far away and have no other option than driving.

professor.name: Professor Nakamura
professor.text: Should universities require all students to take courses outside their major, such as art for engineering students? Why or why not?

students.name: Daniel
students.text: Yes. These courses make students more creative and help them see problems from different angles.

students.name: Mei
students.text: Not necessarily. University is expensive, and students should focus on the skills they need for their careers.

professor.name: Dr. Fischer
professor.text: Social media platforms use algorithms that show users content similar to what they already like. Is this a problem for society? Explain your view.

students.name: Rafael
students.text: Yes. People only see opinions they agree with, which makes society more divided.

students.name: Ingrid
students.text: Not really. People can still choose to follow different sources, and recommendations save time.

professor.name: Professor Okoro
professor.text: Some people believe that it is better to have a stable job with a clear career path, while others prefer to change jobs often to gain different experiences. Which approach is better for young professionals?

students.name: Jamal
students.text: A stable job is better at the beginning. You learn deeply and build a reputation.

students.name: Clara
students.text: Changing jobs is better. You learn more skills and usually get a higher salary each time you move.

professor.name: Dr. Weber
professor.text: Many museums now offer virtual tours online. Can virtual visits replace real visits to museums? Why or why not?

students.name: Hana
students.text: Partly. Virtual tours are great for people who cannot travel, and you can zoom in on details.

students.name: Oliver
students.text: No. Seeing the real size and texture of an artwork is an experience a screen cannot give.

professor.name: Professor Ramirez
professor.text: Should governments tax sugary drinks to reduce health problems like obesity? Explain your position.

students.name: Aisha
students.text: Yes. Taxes on cigarettes reduced smoking, so a similar tax could change people's habits.

students.name: Victor
students.text: No. Adults should make their own choices, and the tax hurts poorer families the most.

professor.name: Dr. Patel
professor.text: Some universities record all lectures and put them online. Does this help students learn, or does it encourage them to skip class?

students.name: Felix
students.text: It helps. I can rewatch difficult parts and review before exams.

students.name: Noor
students.text: Many students stop attending, and they lose the chance to ask questions and discuss with others.

professor.name: Professor Moreau
professor.text: Is it the responsibility of individuals or of large companies to solve environmental problems? Explain your view.

students.name: Ben
students.text: Companies. A few large companies produce most of the pollution, so their decisions matter more.

students.name: Yara
students.text: Both, but individuals have power too. If consumers change what they buy, companies will follow.

professor.name: Dr. Sato
professor.text: Many young people now get their news from short videos rather than newspapers or TV. Is this a positive or negative trend?

students.name: Lucia
students.text: Positive. More young people are interested in the news because the format is attractive.

students.name: Henrik
students.text: Negative. Short videos simplify complex topics and sometimes spread false information.

professor.name: Professor Klein
professor.text: Should employees be allowed to choose their own working hours, as long as they complete their tasks? Why or why not?

students.name: Aria
students.text: Yes. People are productive at different times, and flexibility reduces stress.

students.name: Paolo
students.text: Only partly. Teams need some shared hours to communicate and solve problems together.

professor.name: Dr. Okafor
professor.text: Some people think that space exploration is a waste of money when there are many problems on Earth. Do you agree?

students.name: Kenji
students.text: I disagree. Space research has given us technologies like satellites that help us on Earth.

students.name: Fatima
students.text: I agree to some extent. The money could be used for health and education first.

professor.name: Professor Grant
professor.text: Should high schools teach practical life skills, such as managing money and doing taxes, instead of some traditional subjects?

students.name: Chloe
students.text: Yes. Many young adults don't know how to make a budget, and this causes serious problems.

students.name: Andrei
students.text: These skills are important, but they shouldn't replace subjects like history or literature.

professor.name: Dr. Lindgren
professor.text: Tourism brings money to many cities, but it can also make life harder for residents. Should popular cities limit the number of tourists? Explain.

students.name: Sara
students.text: Yes. In some cities, residents can't afford rent anymore because apartments are rented to tourists.

students.name: Diego
students.text: No. Tourism creates jobs, and limits would hurt small businesses.

professor.name: Professor Adeyemi
professor.text: Is it better for students to specialize early in one field, or to explore many subjects before choosing a major?

students.name: Mia
students.text: Specializing early gives you more time to become an expert.

students.name: Lars
students.text: Exploring is better. Many students choose the wrong field because they decide too early.

professor.name: Dr. Novak
professor.text: Artificial intelligence can now write essays and solve homework problems. Should schools ban students from using AI tools? Why or why not?

students.name: Omar
students.text: Schools should ban them for homework, or students will stop learning to write and think.

students.name: Isabella
students.text: Banning them is unrealistic. Schools should teach students how to use AI responsibly.

professor.name: Professor Hale
professor.text: Some cities are turning car lanes into pedestrian streets. Does this improve city life? Explain your opinion.

students.name: Nina
students.text: Yes. Pedestrian streets are safer and attract cafés and shops.

students.name: Tomasz
students.text: It can make deliveries and access for elderly people more difficult.

professor.name: Dr. Brooks
professor.text: Should companies be required to publish the salaries of all positions to reduce pay inequality? Why or why not?

students.name: Grace
students.text: Yes. Transparency would show unfair differences, for example between men and women.

students.name: Marco
students.text: It might create conflict between colleagues and invade privacy.

professor.name: Professor Wu
professor.text: Is it more important for a leader to be liked or to be respected? Explain your view.

students.name: Hassan
students.text: Respected. A leader sometimes has to make unpopular decisions.

students.name: Julia
students.text: Liked. People work harder for a leader they feel connected to.

professor.name: Dr. Carter
professor.text: Many people buy the latest smartphone every year or two. Should manufacturers be required to make phones that last longer and are easier to repair?

students.name: Ivan
students.text: Yes. Electronic waste is a huge problem, and repairable phones would reduce it.

students.name: Leila
students.text: Consumers should decide. Many people want new features, and that drives innovation.

professor.name: Professor Ellis
professor.text: Should students be required to learn a second foreign language at university? Why or why not?

students.name: Pierre
students.text: Yes. In a global job market, knowing several languages is a major advantage.

students.name: Ana
students.text: It should be optional. Not every career needs it, and the time could be used for other skills.

professor.name: Dr. Ahmed
professor.text: Some argue that online friendships can be as meaningful as face-to-face friendships. Do you agree?

students.name: Zoe
students.text: I agree. Some of my closest friends are people I met in online communities.

students.name: Samuel
students.text: Online friendships lack physical presence. You can't really help each other in difficult moments.

professor.name: Professor Diaz
professor.text: Should public libraries focus more on digital services, like e-books and computer access, than on printed books?

students.name: Rosa
students.text: Yes. Many people now read on devices, and computer access helps those who can't afford one.

students.name: Thomas
students.text: Printed books are still important, especially for children and older readers.

professor.name: Dr. Shah
professor.text: Is it better for governments to invest in high-speed trains or in improving local public transport? Explain.

students.name: Lina
students.text: High-speed trains. They can replace short flights and reduce emissions.

students.name: Jorge
students.text: Local transport. Most people travel short distances every day, not between big cities.

professor.name: Professor Kim
professor.text: Should parents limit the time their teenage children spend online? Why or why not?

students.name: Emma
students.text: Yes. Without limits, teenagers lose sleep and spend less time on physical activities.

students.name: Raj
students.text: Teenagers should learn to manage their own time. Strict limits only create conflict.

professor.name: Dr. Ruiz
professor.text: Many companies hire based on skills tests rather than university degrees. Is a degree still necessary for a successful career?

students.name: Kofi
students.text: Not always. Many successful programmers learned by themselves.

students.name: Valentina
students.text: In many professions, like medicine or law, a degree is essential, and it shows long-term commitment.

professor.name: Professor Bennett
professor.text: Should cities invest more in public art, such as murals and sculptures? Why or why not?

students.name: Lea
students.text: Yes. Public art makes neighborhoods more attractive and gives people a sense of identity.

students.name: Adam
students.text: Cities have more urgent needs, like housing and safety.

professor.name: Dr. Lopez
professor.text: Some experts say that people should be paid for doing household work and caring for family members. Do you agree?

students.name: Sana
students.text: Yes. This work has real economic value, and it is mostly done by women without recognition.

students.name: Erik
students.text: It would be impossible to calculate fairly, and governments can't afford it.

professor.name: Professor Turner
professor.text: Is competition between students in class helpful or harmful for learning? Explain your view.

students.name: Lucas
students.text: Helpful. Competition motivates students to work harder.

students.name: Aiko
students.text: Harmful. It creates stress, and students stop helping each other.

professor.name: Dr. Grant
professor.text: Should fast-food advertising aimed at children be banned? Why or why not?

students.name: Nadia
students.text: Yes. Children cannot judge advertising critically, and these ads contribute to unhealthy eating.

students.name: Paul
students.text: A ban is too extreme. Parents are responsible for what their children eat.

professor.name: Professor Ward
professor.text: Many universities offer courses entirely in English, even in non-English-speaking countries. Is this a good trend?

students.name: Hugo
students.text: Yes. It attracts international students and prepares graduates for global careers.

students.name: Ines
students.text: It can weaken the local language and make learning harder for local students.

professor.name: Dr. Moss
professor.text: Is it a good idea for people to retire later, given that people live longer today? Explain your view.

students.name: Robert
students.text: Yes. People are healthier now, and pension systems need more workers.

students.name: Maya
students.text: Not for physically demanding jobs. A builder cannot work until seventy.

professor.name: Professor Young
professor.text: Should students evaluate their teachers, and should these evaluations affect teachers' careers?

students.name: Anya
students.text: Yes. Students experience the teaching every day, so their opinion is valuable.

students.name: Chris
students.text: Evaluations should be used for feedback, not careers, because students may punish strict teachers.

professor.name: Dr. Stone
professor.text: Some people think that reality TV shows have a negative influence on young viewers. Do you agree?

students.name: Laura
students.text: I agree. These shows often reward rude behavior and promote unrealistic lifestyles.

students.name: Mehmet
students.text: Most viewers know it is entertainment. It is no more harmful than other TV shows.

professor.name: Professor Lane
professor.text: Should employers be allowed to check job applicants' social media profiles? Why or why not?

students.name: Oscar
students.text: Yes. Public posts show how a person behaves and communicates.

students.name: Priya
students.text: No. Private life and professional life should be separate.

professor.name: Dr. Kent
professor.text: Is it better to learn history mainly from textbooks or from visiting historical sites and museums?

students.name: Isaac
students.text: Visiting sites. Seeing the real place makes history memorable.

students.name: Freya
students.text: Textbooks give the full context, which a short visit cannot provide.

professor.name: Professor Hart
professor.text: Many people now use apps to track their health, such as sleep and steps. Do these apps really improve people's health?

students.name: Diana
students.text: Yes. Seeing the numbers motivates me to walk more and sleep earlier.

students.name: Kai
students.text: Some people become anxious about the data, and the apps are not always accurate.

professor.name: Dr. Ross
professor.text: Should wealthy countries accept more climate refugees—people forced to leave their homes because of environmental disasters?

students.name: Amir
students.text: Yes. Rich countries produced most of the emissions, so they have a moral responsibility.

students.name: Clara
students.text: They should help, but mainly by funding protection in affected regions so people can stay.

professor.name: Professor Fox
professor.text: Is working in a team always more effective than working alone? Explain with examples.

students.name: Tim
students.text: Teams are better for complex projects because members bring different skills.

students.name: Selin
students.text: Not always. Creative work like writing is often better done alone.

professor.name: Dr. Page
professor.text: Should plastic packaging be completely banned in supermarkets? Why or why not?

students.name: Mateo
students.text: Yes. Most of it is used once and ends up in the ocean.

students.name: Hanna
students.text: Some packaging keeps food fresh longer, which reduces food waste.

professor.name: Professor Vane
professor.text: Many people believe that the best way to learn about a culture is to live in it. Is it possible to understand a culture without traveling?

students.name: Arjun
students.text: Partly. Films, books and online contact with people can teach a lot.

students.name: Elise
students.text: Not really. Daily habits and values only become clear when you live with people.

professor.name: Dr. Ball
professor.text: Should universities give priority in admission to students from low-income families? Explain your position.

students.name: Jonah
students.text: Yes. It gives equal opportunities to talented students who had fewer resources.

students.name: Lin
students.text: Admission should be based on merit, but universities can offer more scholarships.

professor.name: Professor Cole
professor.text: Is it ethical to keep animals in aquariums and marine parks for education and entertainment?

students.name: Nora
students.text: For entertainment, no. Dolphins performing tricks is cruel.

students.name: Jakub
students.text: Some aquariums do important research and rescue injured animals.

professor.name: Dr. Owen
professor.text: Do you think cash will disappear completely in the future? Would that be a good thing?

students.name: Riya
students.text: Probably, and it would be convenient and safer.

students.name: Stefan
students.text: I hope not. Elderly people and those without bank accounts would be excluded.

professor.name: Professor Ray
professor.text: Should students be required to do an internship before graduating? Why or why not?

students.name: Gabriel
students.text: Yes. Real work experience makes graduates much more employable.

students.name: Yasmin
students.text: It should be encouraged, but many internships are unpaid, which is unfair to poorer students.

professor.name: Dr. Lowe
professor.text: Some people say that modern architecture makes cities look the same everywhere. Should cities protect their traditional style?

students.name: Bianca
students.text: Yes. Traditional buildings give each city its identity.

students.name: Daniel
students.text: Cities need modern buildings to house more people efficiently.

professor.name: Professor Snow
professor.text: Is it a good idea for schools to start later in the morning so that teenagers can sleep more?

students.name: Eva
students.text: Yes. Research shows teenagers' body clocks make early mornings very difficult.

students.name: Kevin
students.text: It would cause problems for parents who need to go to work early.

professor.name: Dr. Hayes
professor.text: Should people be encouraged to grow some of their own food, even in cities? Why or why not?

students.name: Mila
students.text: Yes. Urban gardens provide fresh food and bring neighbors together.

students.name: Andre
students.text: It is a nice hobby, but it cannot really change how cities are fed.

professor.name: Professor Price
professor.text: Some companies offer unlimited vacation days to employees. Is this a good policy? Explain your opinion.

students.name: Lucy
students.text: Yes. It shows trust, and happy employees are more productive.

students.name: Ahmed
students.text: In practice, employees take fewer holidays because they feel pressure not to look lazy.
